title: Impact of nasal HIgh flow therapy on HRQOL on PAtients with COPD and chronic respiratory failure type 1
summary:
The HIPACO-1 study investigates whether nasal high-flow therapy (HFT) in combination with long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) is more beneficial for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and chronic shortness of breath compared to oxygen therapy alone.
For this purpose, 262 patients with severe COPD (stages III or IV) who have been using oxygen at home for at least three months are included in the study. The participants are randomly divided into two groups: one group receives high-flow therapy in addition to oxygen therapy, while the other group continues with oxygen treatment alone. Both groups are observed for a period of one year.
The aim of the study is to find out whether the combination of HFT and LTOT improves the quality of life of patients, particularly with regard to shortness of breath and treatment tolerance. The result is evaluated by questionnaires and regular tests.

interventions.name: HFT for at least 8 hours per day. In addition, the patient receives long-term oxygen treatment (LTOT). A total therapy duration of HFT and LTOT together for at least 16 hours per day is recommended.
Patients assigned to the control group will continue to receive standard care with LTOT. LTOT should be used for a minimum of 16 hours per day.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.    Patients with stage III/IV COPD according to GOLD
2.    Patients receiving long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT) based on a previously diagnosed chronic respiratory insufficiency type I (hypoxemic) or LTOT-naive, hypoxemic patients with an indication for LTOT
3.    Existing LTOT for at least 3 months
4.	Use of LTOT for at least 8 hours per day in the last 4 weeks prior to study inclusion
5.    Guideline-compliant drug treatment of COPD for at least 3 months
Exclusion criteria:
1.    Patients with hypercapnia (PaCO2 > 52 mmHg) and/or acute respiratory acidosis (pH < 7.35)
2.    Presence of a competing cause of chronic respiratory insufficiency type I (hypoxemic)
3.    Patients receiving non-invasive ventilation (NIV), continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), or automatic positive airway pressure (APAP)
4.    Active cancer that may affect the prognosis of the disease
5.    Active smoking
6.    Anemia (hemoglobin < 8.0 g/dl in a BGA)
7.    Severe underlying disease with a life expectancy of < 12 months
8.	Planned rehabilitation treatment in the first 3 months of the study 
9.    Thoracic procedures (endoscopic/surgical) performed within 3 months prior to study entry or pending at the time of study entry
10.    Acute exacerbation of COPD at the time of study entry or in the previous 6 weeks
11.    Patients with previous treatment with HFT in an outpatient setting
12.    Age < 18 years
13.    Simultaneous participation in another clinical intervention study
14.    At the investigator's discretion, participation in the study poses an unacceptable risk due to a pre-existing or concomitant disease or due to the patient's general condition.
15.    The patient is institutionalized due to an administrative or judicial order
16.    Unable to give consent without legal guardianship
17.    Patients who are dependent on or employed by the Coordinating Investigator (Coord. Inv.) or the Principal Investigator (PI)
18.    Patients with private health insurance
